meta.title: Implementing Open Banking for a Youth Banking Platform | Panasa Case Study
meta.description: How Panasa delivered an Open Banking Gateway, parental controls, and PSD2/GDPR-aligned consent and authentication for a UK youth banking platform.

sections.title: Overview
sections.body: Our client is a UK-based youth banking platform that helps children and teenagers manage money under parental oversight. Each child has their own Mastercard-powered debit card and a companion app to track spending, while parents load funds and set controls over merchants and spending categories. The platform is regulated like any other consumer financial product, with the added sensitivity that comes from serving minors.

sections.title: The Challenge
sections.body:
When the UK adopted PSD2, every regulated financial platform including the youth banking platforms had to expose customer account data to authorised Third-Party Providers (TPPs) through a standardised interface, with consent renewed every 90 days.

For a Youth banking platform, this meant that strong customer authentication had to work even if the account holder might be a 10 year old; parental controls and visibility were to be designed as a standard option and account specific information like account details, balance and transaction history were to be available through stable APIs for third party developers regardless of account age or type.

Our client needed a specialist partner who could integrate an Open Banking Gateway, design consent and certification management on top of the existing platform without disrupting the current user experience and in line with GDPR.

sections.title: Struggling with transaction latency?
sections.text: We've optimized processing pipelines from 800ms to under 100ms. Here's how.

sections.title: Our Approach
sections.cardSummary: We structured the implementation across five key areas to deliver a secure, compliant, and user-focused open banking experience for youth banking.

steps.title: Consent Flow
steps.body: Built secure consent journeys with SCA verification, token handling, and automated renewal cycles.

steps.title: Parental Controls
steps.body: Created unified parental permission management with simple access review and revocation.

steps.title: Data Retrieval APIs
steps.body: Standardised APIs ensured consistent account, balance, and transaction data retrieval.

steps.title: Logging & Errors
steps.body: Implemented traceable request logging and developer-friendly error handling workflows.

steps.title: GDPR Compliance
steps.body: Designed consent and data workflows around privacy, revocation, and minimisation principles.

groups.label: OBSERVABILITY
groups.description: Request ID tracing across all API calls, plain-language error translation

groups.label: DATA APIs
groups.description: Certificate-signed API calls, Account listing, balance enquiry, paginated transaction history

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.body: We were able to deliver because we treated Open Banking as a product problem rather than a compliance problem. The common instinct on PSD2 projects is to build a thin compliance shell that satisfies the regulator and leaves the user experience to catch up later. However, what works especially in a category as trust-sensitive as youth banking is designing the consent, SCA and parental control layers as part of the product itself, with the gateway integration sitting underneath them.
